metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (TypeScript) with a deployable entry point (Lambda handler in src/server.ts), a dependency manifest (package.json), and resource-provisioning IaC (infra/template.yaml defining Lambda, DynamoDB, and API Gateway). Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: DynamoDB persistent state with CRUD operations on Product entities (upsert, soft-delete, get, list). Entity lifecycle management (active/inactive status). Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 2.83 yields Partial band but 3 High findings force Remediation Required tier. Strong infrastructure/security/data scores mask critically weak operational practices (no CI/CD, no deployment strategy, no integration testing).

top_gaps.impact: Blocks safe, repeatable deployments; prevents adoption of deployment strategies and security scanning

top_gaps.impact: Production changes carry full blast radius; no canary/blue-green safety net

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists. The service mutates product state (upsert, soft-delete) but does not emit domain events.
findings.gap: No event emission on state mutations. Product creates, updates, and deletes are silent — no downstream systems can react to catalog changes without polling.
findings.recommendation: Add EventBridge integration to emit ProductCreated, ProductUpdated, and ProductDeleted events on mutations. Use DynamoDB Streams with a Lambda trigger to EventBridge for reliable event emission.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: Architecture uses API Gateway as sole ingress with Cognito JWT authorization. Lambda runs in AWS-managed networking accessing DynamoDB via IAM-authenticated API calls. No VPC configuration or VPC endpoints.
findings.gap: No explicit VPC configuration or VPC endpoints. While not strictly required for this serverless architecture, VPC endpoints for DynamoDB would add defense-in-depth.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding a VPC with a DynamoDB VPC endpoint if the service handles sensitive data at scale. Current architecture provides adequate security via API Gateway + Cognito JWT + IAM.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: Lambda provides automatic concurrency scaling and DynamoDB PAY_PER_REQUEST provides automatic capacity scaling. Both layers scale without manual intervention but no explicit concurrency management is configured.
findings.gap: No Lambda concurrency management (ReservedConcurrentExecutions or ProvisionedConcurrency). Traffic spike could exhaust account-level concurrency.
findings.recommendation: Add ReservedConcurrentExecutions to protect against runaway scaling. Consider ProvisionedConcurrency if cold starts affect p99 latency.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: DynamoDB has Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) enabled providing continuous backups with 35-day retention.
findings.gap: No documented restore procedure or tested recovery process. No cross-region backup replication.
findings.recommendation: Document a restore procedure. Consider DynamoDB global tables or cross-region backup for disaster recovery.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: Core infrastructure (Lambda, DynamoDB, API Gateway, IAM, X-Ray) is fully defined in SAM. Missing IaC for monitoring, alerting, and dashboards.
findings.gap: No CloudWatch alarms, dashboards, or operational resources defined in IaC.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms and dashboard resources to the SAM template for Lambda errors, duration, and DynamoDB throttles.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration exists in the repository. Deployments are presumably manual (sam build && sam deploy).
findings.gap: All deployments are manual. No automated build, test, or deploy stages. No automated quality gates.
findings.recommendation: Implement a CI/CD pipeline with stages: lint → build → test → deploy. Use GitHub Actions or AWS CodePipeline with CodeBuild.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: All communication is synchronous. GraphQL queries and mutations execute synchronously against DynamoDB. No async patterns exist for state propagation.
findings.gap: State mutations have no async propagation mechanism. Downstream systems cannot react to catalog changes without polling.
findings.recommendation: Implement domain event emission on mutations via DynamoDB Streams → Lambda → EventBridge.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning strategy is implemented. The GraphQL schema has no version indicator, no @deprecated directives, and no documented evolution strategy.
findings.gap: No versioning strategy means breaking schema changes would affect all consumers simultaneously with no migration path.
findings.recommendation: Implement GraphQL schema evolution strategy: use @deprecated directives, maintain a schema changelog, and consider Apollo Schema Checks for breaking change detection.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: Environment variables used for service configuration (TABLE name via SAM, UserPoolId via parameter). No service registry or dynamic discovery.
findings.gap: Service endpoints configured via environment variables rather than dynamic discovery. Pattern will not scale as services are added.
findings.recommendation: For the current single-service architecture, environment variables are adequate. As ecosystem grows, consider AWS Cloud Map for service discovery.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: All DynamoDB access centralized in src/resolvers/catalog.ts using DynamoDB Document Client. Consistent SDK usage but no formal repository/DAO abstraction.
findings.gap: No explicit data access layer separating business logic from database operations. Resolvers directly couple to DynamoDB SDK specifics.
findings.recommendation: Extract DynamoDB operations into a dedicated repository module (e.g., src/repositories/product.ts) to separate data access from resolver logic.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: DynamoDB has SSE enabled using AWS-managed default encryption key. All data at rest is encrypted.
findings.gap: Uses AWS-managed encryption rather than customer-managed KMS keys. No explicit key rotation policy.
findings.recommendation: Consider upgrading to customer-managed KMS key with automatic key rotation for sensitive product data.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: Lambda runtime (nodejs20.x) is automatically patched by AWS. arm64 Graviton architecture. No application-level dependency vulnerability scanning.
findings.gap: No dependency vulnerability scanning. Application dependencies (npm packages) not scanned for known vulnerabilities. No lock file for reproducible builds.
findings.recommendation: Add npm audit to build process. Add package-lock.json. Consider Snyk for continuous dependency monitoring.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists, so no security scanning tools are integrated. No SAST, no dependency scanning, no Dependabot configuration.
findings.gap: Zero security validation in delivery process. Dependency vulnerabilities and code-level security issues reach production undetected.
findings.recommendation: When implementing CI/CD, include npm audit as blocking gate, SAST tool (Semgrep or CodeGuru Reviewer), and Dependabot for automated dependency updates.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: X-Ray tracing enabled at Lambda function level (Tracing: Active). Automatic tracing of Lambda invocations and DynamoDB calls. No custom segments or business-context annotations.
findings.gap: Tracing is infrastructure-level only without business-context enrichment (product SKU, operation type annotations).
findings.recommendation: Add X-Ray subsegments with annotations in resolver code to enrich traces with business context.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLO definitions exist. No CloudWatch alarms on latency, error rate, or availability. No error budget tracking.
findings.gap: No measurable service-level targets. Cannot determine whether service is meeting user expectations.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs: availability 99.9%, query latency p99 < 200ms, error rate < 0.1%. Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom business metrics published. No CloudWatch putMetricData calls for business events. Only default Lambda and DynamoDB infrastructure metrics available.
findings.gap: Cannot measure business outcomes — only infrastructure health. Cannot answer business questions from metrics.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics using Embedded Metric Format: products_created, products_updated, products_deleted, catalog_queries.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms (static or anomaly), no SNS topics, no incident notification integration.
findings.gap: Service failures and degradation go undetected until users report issues.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms: Lambda Errors > 0, Duration p99 > 5000ms, DynamoDB SystemErrors > 0. Add anomaly detection on latency. Route to SNS topic.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy
findings.description: No deployment strategy configured. Lambda function has no DeploymentPreference. Deployments are manual sam deploy with no traffic shifting or rollback.
findings.gap: Direct-to-production deployments with no staged rollout. Bad deployment affects 100% of traffic immediately.
findings.recommendation: Add DeploymentPreference: Type: Canary10Percent5Minutes with CloudWatch alarms as rollback triggers.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No test files exist despite vitest being configured as devDependency. Zero automated test coverage for GraphQL resolvers and DynamoDB interactions.
findings.gap: No regression safety net. Code changes cannot be validated automatically.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests using vitest: test CRUD operations against DynamoDB Local or mocked client. Add contract tests for GraphQL schema.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation
findings.description: No incident response automation. No runbooks, no SSM Automation documents, no self-healing workflows.
findings.gap: No documented or automated response to common failure scenarios. Recovery depends on manual investigation.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common scenarios: DynamoDB throttling, Lambda errors, auth failures. Consider SSM Automation for automated remediation.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership artifacts. No CODEOWNERS, no per-service dashboards, no alarms with named owners.
findings.gap: No defined ownership of service health. Monitoring gaps likely because no team is accountable.
findings.recommendation: Add CODEOWNERS file. Define CloudWatch dashboards in IaC with team attribution tags. Document on-call ownership.

findings.title: Resource Tagging Governance
findings.description: No resource tags defined on any AWS resource in the SAM template. Lambda, DynamoDB, and API Gateway have no tags.
findings.gap: Cannot track costs per workload, identify resource ownership, or enforce environment-based policies.
findings.recommendation: Add tags to all resources: Environment, Service, Team, CostCenter. Use SAM Globals or per-resource Tags properties.

evaluations.title: Managed Compute
evaluations.reason: All compute on Lambda (serverless) with nodejs20.x on arm64. No EC2.

evaluations.title: Managed Databases
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB fully managed with PAY_PER_REQUEST, SSE, and PITR.

evaluations.title: Workflow Orchestration
evaluations.reason: No multi-step workflows exist in this CRUD service. All operations are single DynamoDB calls.

evaluations.title: API Entry Point
evaluations.reason: HTTP API Gateway with Cognito JWT authorizer, built-in throttling, and request routing.

evaluations.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
evaluations.reason: All components (Lambda, DynamoDB, API Gateway) are inherently multi-AZ.

evaluations.title: Programming Languages
evaluations.reason: TypeScript 5.4+ on Node.js 20 with AWS SDK v3 and Apollo Server 4.

evaluations.title: Monolith vs Microservices
evaluations.reason: Single-purpose microservice with well-defined boundaries, own data store, clear API contract.

evaluations.title: Long-Running Process Handling
evaluations.reason: No operations exceed 30 seconds. All operations are single DynamoDB API calls with 30s Lambda timeout.

evaluations.title: Unstructured Data Storage
evaluations.reason: Service handles structured product data only. No unstructured data to manage.

evaluations.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB is fully managed with no user-configurable engine version. No EOL risk.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: No stored procedures. DynamoDB NoSQL with all business logic in application layer.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Application-level IaC only. CloudTrail is an account-level concern belonging in foundation infrastructure repo.

evaluations.title: API Authentication
evaluations.reason: Two-layer auth: API Gateway Cognito JWT authorizer + resolver scope checks (catalog:write).

evaluations.title: Centralized Identity Integration
evaluations.reason: Integrates with Amazon Cognito as centralized IdP. External User Pool referenced via parameter.

evaluations.title: Secrets Management
evaluations.reason: No secrets to manage. DynamoDB access via IAM roles. No credentials in code.
